summary: The JavaScript movement preflight and trap selector omit the hero LEVEL_TELEP arm, and teleport.c:dotele still records level_tele_trap as unported. The selected recording only reaches trap.c:dotrap’s known-trap rn2(5) escape arm (C draws 0), so source completion also requires independent matching evidence for natural unseen-trap activation and the #teleport command on a known trap.

source.branch: When the hero activates a LEVEL_TELEP trap, trap.c:trapeffect_level_telep calls seetrap then teleport.c:level_tele_trap; when the hero invokes dotelecmd on a seen LEVEL_TELEP square, teleport.c:dotele asks for confirmation and calls level_tele_trap with FORCETRAP, spending a turn whether relocation works or not. For natural activation, trap.c:dotrap first handles the known-trap escape roll; a hidden trap or a seen trap whose rn2(5) roll does not escape reaches the effect selector.
callers: hack.c:domove_core -> requireSimpleHeroDestination -> spoteffects -> trap.c:dotrap -> trapeffect_selector -> trap.c:trapeffect_level_telep -> teleport.c:level_tele_trap; JavaScript already wires the preflight and production caller, but preflight_dotrap excludes LEVEL_TELEP and the effect helper refuses the hero arm.

teleport.c:dotelecmd calls dotele and maps its boolean return to ECMD_TIME or ECMD_OK; cmd.c binds both #teleport and Ctrl-T to dotelecmd, and the JavaScript command dispatcher already reaches that handler.
trap.c:drown calls dotele(FALSE) from the drowning escape path; this existing caller belongs to A2’s reserved trap.c:drown task and is a read-only caller frontier here.
dig.c:escape_tomb calls dotele(FALSE), but a repository-wide C caller search finds no active call to escape_tomb().
dependencies: trap.c:trapeffect_level_telep is the source caller required for the natural LEVEL_TELEP effect; its monster arm and teleport.c:mlevel_tele_trap dependency are already ported, so preserve them while completing the hero arm.
teleport.c:level_tele() and display.c:shieldeff() are existing implementations used by level_tele_trap; the new helper consumes no C callee return value.

evidence: The saved v47 evaluation at challenges/evaluations/baseline-a6e3a17cc-v47.json records 46/48 screens, 3418/3437 RNG values, and 46/48 cursors. The first JS stop is at segment 0 step 46 on the move input: UnsupportedHeroMoveBoundaryError('trap activation'). The recipe/recording identities are challenges/cases/v47/v47-hero-level-teleport-trap-attempt6-attempt8-datetime-corrected.recipe.session.json (a1cc9e7f73f380935122004f3656e756941c4aea5569f1a3840c27b2b6e44a73) and challenges/cases/v47/v47-hero-level-teleport-trap-attempt6-attempt8-datetime-corrected.session.json (f8ecd42405608bc3a91186f5a85d41eb6ddc7ee068f5474c64aaa85d33fcb673).

A fresh differential from the worker base with saved-queue identity 46b5891629d3d59e5e62550cd812381e88752c80574406c65acffb4f4fed55cb showed the first C-only RNG call at segment 0 step 47 after confirmation: rn2(5)=0 at trap.c:3038. C then prints “You escape a level teleporter.” Because that roll escapes before effect selection, the admitted recording does not execute trapeffect_level_telep or level_tele_trap.

Upstream hack.c:domove_core checks the destination trap through the hero movement preflight before moving; after movement hack.c:spoteffects calls dotrap for a trap under the hero. trap.c:dotrap:3035-3043 handles the known-trap escape roll, then its final dispatch at 3059 calls trapeffect_selector; selector:2966-2967 dispatches LEVEL_TELEP to trapeffect_level_telep.

Upstream trap.c:trapeffect_level_telep:2088-2105 calls seetrap() before teleport.c:level_tele_trap() for the hero and returns Trap_Effect_Finished; its nonhero arm delegates to mlevel_tele_trap and maps that return. In js/trap_effects.js the nonhero arm is ported, but the hero arm throws unsupported and preflight_dotrap excludes LEVEL_TELEP at both the type whitelist and seen-trap gate.

Upstream teleport.c:dotele:1034-1164 first ignores unseen traps; for a seen LEVEL_TELEP it prompts and calls level_tele_trap(trap, FORCETRAP), then returns 1. js/teleport.js:dotele currently records note_unported(teleport.c level_tele_trap) and returns 1. Its production direct caller is dotelecmd; trap.c:drown is a separate active caller owned by A2 and requires no edit here.

Upstream teleport.c:level_tele_trap:1538-1574 chooses “trigger” and marks the path intentional for VIASITTING/FORCETRAP, otherwise describes locomotion onto the trap; natural antimagic shields and returns with a wrenching message, and In_endgame also returns without deletion. Otherwise it deletes/redraws the trap, calls level_tele(), reports orientation or disorientation, then applies temporary confusion only without Teleport_control. These source-order effects have no return-dependent unported callee.

Independent runtime evidence will use a wizard terrain wish for an initially unseen LEVEL_TELEP, step away, and re-enter so the ordinary movement path reaches the natural helper. A separate recording will source-reveal a wished trap, stand on its seen square, and use #teleport to exercise dotelecmd -> dotele -> level_tele_trap(FORCETRAP); neither recipe will reuse the selected challenge inputs.
